title: Malooga
subtitle: Yemeni layered flatbread with butter lamination, pan-fried
excerpt: Malooga is a thin, flaky Yemeni flatbread made by layering butter between stretched sheets of yeasted dough, then folding and frying in a dry pan or on a griddle. The result is something between a paratha and a pastry: richly flavoured, with visible flaky layers and a golden, slightly blistered surface. It is traditionally eaten for breakfast with honey and butter or alongside Yemeni fenugreek dip.
sourceNotes: Malooga is a traditional Yemeni bread, the pan-fried layered version closely related to malawach (a Yemeni Jewish laminated flatbread brought to Israel in the 1950s). Both derive from the same Yemeni flatbread tradition. The technique of repeatedly folding butter or clarified butter into a yeasted dough to create layers is shared with Indian paratha and other laminated flatbreads across South and West Asia. The recipe is documented in Yemeni food references and the diaspora cookery tradition.

content.text: Malooga layers are created by spreading soft butter over the stretched dough, then folding and rolling several times to build multiple buttery sheets. The dough should be soft and very pliable; stiff dough tears rather than stretching thinly. Fry over a steady medium heat: too high and the outside burns before the layers cook through; too low and the bread is oily rather than flaky.

Combine {{plain-flour}}, {{yeast-fast-action}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{caster-sugar}} in a large bowl. Add {{water}} and {{vegetable-oil}} and mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and pliable. Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and leave for 1 hour until doubled.

Divide the dough into 6 equal portions (about 110 g each). Round each into a ball, place on an oiled surface, cover with cling film, and rest for 30 minutes. Resting relaxes the gluten so the dough stretches without springing back.

Working one at a time, roll a dough ball on a lightly oiled surface into a thin round, about 25 cm across. Spread a heaped teaspoon of {{unsalted-butter}} over the surface, almost to the edges. Fold the round in thirds like a letter, then fold again into a smaller square. You now have a multilayered packet. Roll this out again to a rough round about 18 to 20 cm across. Repeat with the remaining balls.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat with no oil. Cook each malooga for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden patches appear and the edges begin to look dry. The bread puffs slightly in the pan; press down gently with a spatula to ensure even contact. Serve hot with honey and butter, or alongside soup or stew.
